material.notes: More ductile than PLA; better interlayer adhesion. Lower stiffness — deflection-limited designs may need thicker sections.

forces.comment: Full Yeti bottle (~1.5kg incl. water) resting in the cradle; y=bo_cy (cradle centerline), z arbitrary mid-cradle-height (gravity moment about the X bending axis depends only on the Y offset for this geometry, not Z).
Kindle in its channel (0.2kg), y = mid-channel centroid (y_k0..y_k1 midpoint).
iPhone in case, in its channel (0.25kg), y = mid-channel centroid (y_p0..y_p1 midpoint).

Caddy self-weight (0.5kg est., base+spine+gussets+haunches+cradle wall). Y-centroid ~50mm from the root, volume-weighted across spine (heavy, at the very back), gussets (triangular, centroid at 1/3 of their 170mm run), base plate (uniform across full depth), and bottle-cradle wall — cross-checked against the spec narrative estimate of ~1.5-2 N*m total overturning moment (this force set sums to ~1.83 N*m at the root, consistent).

sections.name: root-spine-mount-junction
sections.comment: Full-width solid spine block (caddy_w x spine_h) at y=0, the base<->spine/mount junction named in the design brief as the peak-moment section. Printed base-down per the v3 directive, so the peak tensile/compressive fiber (top/bottom of this section) runs fore-aft (Y) = in-plane with the horizontal layers, not interlayer peel. This model captures ONLY the solid spine block; it deliberately ignores the two side buttress gussets and the back-corner haunches (extra, unquantified reinforcement) that also cross this junction, so it is a conservative FLOOR on the true section strength, not the true composite. Not a clean prism once gussets/haunches are counted -> FEA recommended for an exact composite number, though the margin here should be enormous given the base_t/spine_t upsizing.

sections.name: gusset-taper-post-spine
sections.comment: Idealizes the TWO side buttress gussets alone (each 4.5mm thick x taper height, combined as one 9mm-wide equivalent rect since gusset X-position does not affect bending resistance about the X axis) at y=9mm, just aft of the spine, where the spine's full 140x110 block ends and the tapering gusset+base-plate composite becomes the sole flexural member for the rest of the cantilever (y=9..170). Height 70.5mm = linear taper value at y=9 (gusset_h=74mm at y=0 -> 0 at y=170, per side_gusset() polygon). Deliberately ignores the 5.5mm base plate and haunch fillets underneath (extra, unquantified reinforcement) -> conservative FLOOR. Gussets print as vertical ribs, base-down, so bending stress (fore-aft) runs in-plane with horizontal layers, not interlayer peel. Not a clean prism (two separate outboard ribs, not a solid block) -> FEA recommended for an exact composite number. Hand-swept check across y=9..160 (not run through this single-point CLI section) shows stress stays under ~0.22 MPa throughout this region -- well below either candidate section here -- so no additional mid-span section is expected to govern.
